story.title: Kenya Discharges Last Ebola Patient, Starts 42-Day Countdown to Ebola-Free Status
story.summary: Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient, marking a significant milestone in the country's efforts to combat the virus. This event initiates a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free, contingent on the absence of new cases during this period.

timeline_highlights.title: Congolese Politician Beaten After Promoting Ebola Awareness
timeline_highlights.summary: Marie-Celestin Karondwa, a politician from the ruling UDPS party in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, was beaten on Sunday after advocating for Ebola awareness during a radio interview. The incident occurred in Butembo, a region experiencing an Ebola outbreak, as residents reacted violently to his message promoting disease prevention measures.
key_facts: Marie-Celestin Karondwa was a member of the UDPS party.
He was attacked after a radio interview about Ebola awareness.
The incident took place in Butembo, North Kivu province.

timeline_highlights.title: Ebola Death Toll in Congo Exceeds 5,000 Amid Widespread Concerns
timeline_highlights.summary: The Ebola outbreak in Congo has resulted in over 5,000 deaths, with the latest figures from the Congolese Ministry of Health reporting 5,026 fatalities among 10,351 infections, indicating a nearly 50% lethality rate. The situation has raised fears of the disease spreading to other African nations as new cases are being recorded.

timeline_highlights.title: British Healthcare Worker with Ebola Evacuated to UK for Treatment
timeline_highlights.summary: A British healthcare worker in the Democratic Republic of Congo has tested positive for Ebola and is being evacuated to the UK for treatment. The patient is reported to be in stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist infectious disease unit. The UK government has confirmed the evacuation and stated that established procedures are in place for handling such cases.

event_overview.title: About Awareness Outbreak
event_overview.subject: Awareness Outbreak
event_overview.summary: “Awareness Outbreak” refers to the 2026 Ebola disease emergency caused by Bundibugyo virus, centered in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and managed through national and international public-health response systems. Declared in May 2026, it has involved cross-border preparedness and imported-case responses in neighboring countries, while community engagement, testing, contact tracing and safe-care measures have been central to efforts to interrupt transmission.

facts.label: Start and international status
facts.value: The DRC declared the outbreak on 15 May 2026; WHO determined it to be a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, activating international coordination under the International Health Regulations.

facts.label: Disease involved
facts.value: The event concerns Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus (Bundibugyo virus disease), rather than the more common Ebola Zaire virus. WHO states that there was no approved vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo virus disease; care and control relied principally on early detection, isolation, supportive care and public-health measures.

facts.label: Geographic focus
facts.value: The outbreak began in northeastern DRC, with Ituri Province the epicentre, and expanded across multiple DRC provinces. WHO also documented cross-border spread or preparedness needs, including Uganda; Kenya later reported an imported case linked to travel from the DRC.

facts.label: Response leadership and methods
facts.value: DRC and Ugandan health authorities activated emergency coordination and response operations with WHO and partners. Core measures include surveillance, laboratory testing, infection prevention and control, clinical management, contact tracing, safe burials, cross-border coordination and community engagement.

facts.label: Why public awareness is material
facts.value: WHO identifies community engagement as essential to controlling this outbreak, particularly given insecurity, displacement, mobile populations and barriers to timely detection and access to care in affected areas.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline highlights particular late-September and October 2026 developments—especially awareness efforts, laboratory capacity, mortality reporting, and Kenya’s imported-case response—but it does not constitute a complete epidemiological record of the wider DRC-centered outbreak or every affected country.

related_stories.title: 74-Year-Old Kidnapper Escapes House Arrest in Argentina
related_stories.summary: Leonardo Bertulazzi, a 74-year-old former member of the Red Brigades, escaped from house arrest in Buenos Aires, Argentina. He was awaiting extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence. Authorities confirmed his escape, which reportedly involved him using a harness to abseil from a balcony.

related_stories.title: New Israeli Parliament Sworn In Amid Netanyahu's Caretaker Leadership
related_stories.summary: A new Israeli parliament was sworn in, with Gadi Eisenkot, the politician tasked with forming a government, vowing to reverse many of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies. The first session of the parliament saw Eisenkot and his allies launching a legislative challenge against Netanyahu's legacy.
